expectations.text: Refuses to present 31,400 downloads as organizations or as usage, stating downloads measure install interest only.
States that only in-server telemetry answers the adoption question, and that download counts exclude private mirrors and cannot be read as execution counts.
expectations.evidence: "They include CI re-installs and private mirrors... Only in-server telemetry measures usage."

expectations.text: Rejects registry listing or directory rank as a trust or security claim, stating the official registry is a metadata catalog with namespace-ownership proof and community moderation that certifies nothing about security.
expectations.evidence: "metadata catalog with DNS namespace-ownership proof... certifies nothing about security."

expectations.text: Prescribes instrumenting tool calls as OpenTelemetry spans - session to tool invocation to downstream operation - rather than a bespoke event schema.
Justifies OpenTelemetry by the enterprise customer's own observability stack being an audience for the data, not only Pellham's dashboard.
Names the metric set: call volume, success and error rate, per-tool usage, active users, and client distribution.
expectations.evidence: Lists distinct orgs, tool calls per week, error rate only; no per-tool usage or client distribution.

expectations.text: States the dual purpose of that metric set - confirming the server is used at all, and whether adoption is broad or concentrated.
Handles the gateway-fronted customers by designing metrics to be correlatable through stable tool names and request IDs, instead of assuming Pellham's telemetry is the only visibility layer.
expectations.evidence: "We've made our tool names and request IDs correlatable and asked them for gateway-side counts."

expectations.text: Points at the first-party disclosure shape worth matching - call volume, write share, non-technical-user share, enterprise share, retention by cohort, and accuracy plus token-efficiency gains.
